afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 251112
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
412 AM MST Wed Nov 25 2026

.UPDATE...Updated Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and tranquil weather will persist through at least the 
  weekend as temperatures gradually warm into a slightly above 
  normal range. 

- Periods of breezy conditions over high terrain areas and along 
  the lower Colorado River Valley will be common the next couple 
  days. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
The forecast through the holiday weekend remains on track with
very little change in the air mass and temperatures running 
anywhere from 3-8 degrees above normal. Dry conditions remain in 
place with shortwave ridging currently progressing through the 
region. However, just upstream to the northwest, a fast moving 
shortwave trough is nearing the southern and central coast of 
California. This system is already losing most of its moisture and
as it brushes past our region to the southwest it will only bring
some semi-thick high level clouds for our area today into 
tonight.

Although the incoming system will mostly brush by to the 
southwest, it is already increasing the pressure gradient across 
the area. Expect breezy east winds across the eastern Arizona high
terrain this morning and again Thursday morning and northwesterly
breezy winds tonight and Thursday across southeast California and
far western Arizona. By early Thursday, an even stronger Pacific 
ridge will begin begin to overtake the region from the west 
quickly raising H5 heights to as high as 585-588dm Thursday night 
into Friday. Temperatures will continue to tick upward over the 
next couple of days with much of the lower deserts reaching the 
mid 70s today and upper 70s starting Thursday.

&&

.LONG TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/... 
The upcoming weekend calls for the Pacific ridge to remain 
dominant across our region, but it will be in a weakening phase 
and is likely to get knocked down by a fast moving disturbance 
passing across the Four Corners area. Even with H5 heights 
dropping to between 580-583dm, temperatures are not expected to 
drop much with lower desert highs at least maintaining mid 70s for
highs. The weather pattern suggests another brief shortwave ridge
moving through on Monday and/or Tuesday, but models are favoring 
a gradual increase in moisture early next week pushing PWAT 
anomalies to around 150-175% of normal by Tuesday. Temperatures 
are not expected to change much early next week despite the 
expected increase in clouds. Models then favor a more significant
Pacific disturbance approaching the California coast and then 
likely passing through our region during the middle of next week. 
The timing, strength, and exact track of the system is still quite
uncertain, but there are at least decent signs it will contain 
adequate moisture for some precipitation chances for our region. 
We expect it will be at least a few more days until we have a good
idea on rain potential for next week's weather system.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1115Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Uncertainty and variability in wind direction will be the main
weather concern through Thursday morning under frequent high
cirrus decks. Confidence is good that an E/NE wind component will
prevail the majority of the period, however, large variability
will be possible through the period. For example, winds have
developed the typical cold season counter-intuitive light SW
component at KPHX early this morning, which may continue for
several hours. This may occur once again tonight into early
Thursday morning, but is not included in the current TAF. By
16-18Z this morning, E/NE winds should reestablish and become
briefly gusty into the mid teens across some of the terminals.
Confidence is also low regarding wind directions late this
afternoon, as trajectories may attempt to become N/NW for a few
hours around sunset. However, Hi-Res guidance indicates that E/NE
winds could persist through the afternoon and evening. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No weather concerns will exist through the next 24 hours under
increasing high cirrus decks. Confidence is very good that winds
will behave similarly to the past 24 hours, and generally vary
between westerly and northerly directions. Extended periods of
variability to nearly calm conditions will be common. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry and tranquil conditions will continue across the region. 
Temperatures will warm to above normal by Thursday region wide and 
remain around 4-7 degrees above normal through the weekend. MinRH's 
will range between 15-30% through most of the forecast period, while 
cool overnight lows will result in decent to good overnight recovery 
each night. Outside of periods of marginally breezy conditions over 
AZ high terrain areas and the Lower Colorado River Valley (mainly 
today through Thursday), light winds will be favored.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...Updated 11/23 1933Z.
Gila River: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area due to continued water releases upwards of 
3000 cfs. Water levels near Dateland continue to rise, with gauge 
data now showing a depth of just above 7 ft and flow exceeding 1100 
cfs. At the current rate of rise, the water level at the Dateland 
gauge is expected to reach action stage (8 ft) by Thursday-Friday. A 
separate Flood Warning segment remains in effect from Dateland to 
Yuma. These water levels will have the potential to flood farm 
fields and low water crossings along the river downstream from the 
dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Kuhlman
LONG TERM...Kuhlman
AVIATION...Whittock/18
FIRE WEATHER...Berislavich
HYDROLOGY...Benedict/RW
